member.name: M:Mutagen.Bethesda.Plugins.Analysis.DI.MultiModFileSplitter.OrderCreatedClusters``2(System.Collections.Generic.Dictionary{Mutagen.Bethesda.Plugins.FormKey,Mutagen.Bethesda.Plugins.Analysis.DI.MultiModFileSplitter.AnalyzedRecord{``0,``1}})
member.summary: Tarjan strongly-connected-components over the created-record reference graph. Each component becomes a cluster of records that must share a mod fragment, returned in dependency-first order (a cluster is emitted only after everything it references). Edges: a created record to each created record it links to, plus bidirectional edges across created parent chains so a created parent and its created children always share a cluster.

Reserves the mod fragment for a set of external masters and referenced formkeys: the first mod fragment that can hold it without exceeding the master limit and without referencing a later mod fragment, else a new mod fragment. The unit's masters are registered on the chosen mod fragment.

member.name: T:Mutagen.Bethesda.Plugins.Binary.Parameters.ALowerRangeDisallowedHandlerOption
member.summary:
A class representing how to handle when lower formID ranges are used in a non-allowed way.
Typically this occurs when the lower ranges are used without any masters present
Options:
NoCheckIfLowerRangeDisallowed ThrowIfLowerRangeDisallowed AddPlaceholderMasterIfLowerRangeDisallowed

member.name: T:Mutagen.Bethesda.Plugins.Binary.Parameters.NoCheckIfLowerRangeDisallowed
member.summary:
A class representing how to handle when lower formID ranges are used in a non-allowed way.
Typically this occurs when the lower ranges are used without any masters present.
This option skips any checking of this situation

member.name: T:Mutagen.Bethesda.Plugins.Binary.Parameters.ThrowIfLowerRangeDisallowed
member.summary:
A class representing how to handle when lower formID ranges are used in a non-allowed way.
Typically this occurs when the lower ranges are used without any masters present.
If this occurs with this option, an exception will be thrown

member.name: T:Mutagen.Bethesda.Plugins.Binary.Parameters.AddPlaceholderMasterIfLowerRangeDisallowed
member.summary:
A class representing how to handle when lower formID ranges are used in a non-allowed way.
Typically this occurs when the lower ranges are used without any masters present.
If this occurs with this option, the base mod (first on the load order) will be added as a placeholder. If no load order exists, then an exception will be thrown

member.summary: For use when a previously encountered record is seen again

Writes a set of sibling GRUPs that share a merge key (GroupType + Label). - If there's one sibling, emits it, recursing into its sub-groups so nested duplicates are still merged. - If multiple, emits the last sibling's header (preserving its label/last-modified stamp), then merges their contents. For leaf groups, contents are concatenated. For container groups (content begins with GRUP), children from every sibling are gathered, re-grouped by their merge key, and recursively processed — so duplicates at any depth get merged.

member.name: M:Mutagen.Bethesda.Plugins.Binary.Translations.BinaryReadBuilder`3.Construct
member.summary:
Executes the instructions to read the mod into a readonly object.
This is a lazy loading object, with does minimal work up front, and does any parsing work as fields are accessed.
There is no caching, so every access will reparse the data.
If you want a mutable version of the mod, call Mutable() first.
member.returns: A readonly mod object with minimal initial parsing done

Note that this loads in the entire mod up front, which takes longer and uses more memory.
Use this call only if you intend to mutate the mod after loading it, otherwise use the non-mutable alternative.

Separated master games (like Starfield) need to know what their masters styles are in order to parse correctly, which is normally retrieved via looking at the mod files themselves from the Data Folder.
This is an alternative to hand provide the information so that they do not need to be present in the Data folder

Retrieves the winning EditorID that matches the FormKey relative to the source the cache was attached to.
If a record exists that matches the FormKey, but does not inherit from the given generic, it will not be returned, and the function will return false.
NOTE: This call is much slower than the alternative that uses generics, as all records in the entire mod must be processed, rather than being able to scope the search to a specific area.
member.param: Out parameter containing the EditorID if successful
member.returns: True if a matching record was found

member.name: T:Mutagen.Bethesda.Plugins.Cache.Internals.Implementations.ImmutableLoadOrderLinkCache
member.summary:
A Link Cache using a LoadOrder as its link target.
Will resolve links to the highest overriding mod containing the record being sought.
Internal caching will only occur as deep into the load order as necessary, for only the types required to serve the requested link.
All functionality is multithread safe.
Modification of the target LoadOrder, or Mods on the LoadOrder is not safe. Internal caches can become incorrect if modifications occur on content already cached.

member.summary:
Retrieves the winning record context that matches the FormKey relative to the source the cache was attached to.
If a record exists that matches the FormKey, but does not inherit from the given generic, it will not be returned, and the function will throw a MissingRecordException.
NOTE: This call is much slower than the alternative that uses generics, as all records in the entire mod must be processed, rather than being able to scope the search to a specific area.
member.exception: When the FormKey cannot be found under the attached cache.

member.name: T:Mutagen.Bethesda.Plugins.Cache.LinkCacheFromModMixIn
member.summary:
Extension methods that resolve records against the contribution of one specific mod within a cache, located by its ModKey.
Unlike or resolution, these methods do not search the load order for the winning override or the origin definition. They instead scope resolution to the record as it exists within the single mod matching the given ModKey.
If the cache does not contain a mod matching the given ModKey, the Try variants return false and the throwing variants throw a .

member.summary:
A pairing of a record as well as the logic and knowledge of where it came from in its parent mod. This allows a context to insert the record into a new mod, using the knowledge to properly insert and find the appropriate location within the new mod.
This is typically only useful for deeper nested records such as Cell/PlacedObjects/Navmeshes/etc

member.summary:
Will find and return the most overridden version of each record in the list of mods of the given type.
Additionally, it will come wrapped in a context object that has knowledge of where each record came from.
This context helps when trying to override deep records such as Cells/PlacedObjects/etc, as the context is able to navigate and insert the record into the proper location for you.
This system is overkill for simpler top-level records.

Getter Mod type to target

member.name: M:Mutagen.Bethesda.Plugins.IWinningOverrideProvider`2.WinningContextOverrides(Mutagen.Bethesda.Plugins.Cache.ILinkCache,System.Type,System.Boolean)
member.summary:
Will find and return the most overridden version of each record in the list of mods of the given type.
Additionally, it will come wrapped in a context object that has knowledge of where each record came from.
This context helps when trying to override deep records such as Cells/PlacedObjects/etc, as the context is able to navigate and insert the record into the proper location for you.
This system is overkill for simpler top-level records.
member.typeparam: Setter Mod type to target
Getter Mod type to target
member.param: LinkCache to use when creating parent objects

Type of record to search for and iterate.
USAGE NOTE:
Typically you should only supply the Getter interfaces for the type.
A setter interface being given can result in no records being found, as most LoadOrders are readonly.
Whether to include deleted records in the output
member.returns: Enumerable of the most overridden version of each record of the given type, optionally including deleted ones

Returns a FormKey with the next listed ID in the Mod's header. No checks will be done that this is truly a unique key; It is assumed the header is in a correct state.

member.name: T:Mutagen.Bethesda.Plugins.FormID
member.summary:
A struct representing a FormID. It wraps a raw uint, and exposes sections of it depending on if it's a normal, light, or medium FormID.
Note: FormID should be used sparingly, as it's prone to Mod indexing errors if mishandled. FormKey is a more preferable struct for normal use.

member.name: T:Mutagen.Bethesda.Plugins.FormKey
member.summary:
A struct representing a unique identifier for a record:
- The ID of a record (6 bytes)
- The ModKey the record originates from
FormKeys are preferable to FormIDs, as they:
- Cannot be misinterpreted to originate from the wrong Mod depending on context
- Remove the 255 limit while within code space. On-disk formats still enforce 255 limit.

member.exception: If the FormKey's ModKey is not present in the mod's masters

member.returns: True if a matching record was found

member.name: M:Mutagen.Bethesda.DuplicateFromMixIn.DuplicateFromOnlyReferenced``2(``0,Mutagen.Bethesda.Plugins.Cache.ILinkCache{``0,``1},Mutagen.Bethesda.Plugins.ModKey,System.Type[])
member.summary:
Duplicates records into a given mod 'modToDuplicateInto', which originated from target ModKey 'modKeyToDuplicateFrom'.
Only considers records that are currently within the target modToDuplicateInto, which are then duplicated.
Records from the modKeyToDuplicateFrom that are not within or referenced by records in the target mod are skipped.
End result will be that all records that the given modToDuplicateInto contains or references that originate from the target modKeyToDuplicateFrom will be duplicated in and replace the records they duplicated. No references to the modKeyToDuplicateFrom will remain.
member.param: Mod to duplicate into and originate new records from
ModKey to search modToDuplicateInto for, and duplicate records that originate from modKeyToDuplicateFrom

Types to iterate and look at within modToDuplicateInto for references to modKeyToDuplicateFrom
Only use if you know specifically the types that can reference modKeyToDuplicateFrom, and want a little bit of speed by not checking uninteresting records.

member.name: M:Mutagen.Bethesda.OverrideMixIns.WinningContextOverrides``4(System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable{Mutagen.Bethesda.Plugins.Order.IModListingGetter{``1}},Mutagen.Bethesda.Plugins.Cache.ILinkCache,System.Boolean)
member.summary:
Will find and return the most overridden version of each record in the list of mods of the given type.
Additionally, it will come wrapped in a context object that has knowledge of where each record came from.
This context helps when trying to override deep records such as Cells/PlacedObjects/etc, as the context is able to navigate and insert the record into the proper location for you.
This system is overkill for simpler top-level records.

member.name: M:Mutagen.Bethesda.OverrideMixIns.WinningContextOverrides``2(System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable{Mutagen.Bethesda.Plugins.Order.IModListingGetter{``1}},Mutagen.Bethesda.Plugins.Cache.ILinkCache,System.Type,System.Boolean)
member.summary:
Will find and return the most overridden version of each record in the list of mods of the given type.
Additionally, it will come wrapped in a context object that has knowledge of where each record came from.
This context helps when trying to override deep records such as Cells/PlacedObjects/etc, as the context is able to navigate and insert the record into the proper location for you.
This system is overkill for simpler top-level records.
